message.content: In Christian tradition, the emphasis is often on Jesus Christ as the central and ultimate figure—many Christians view Him as the fulfillment of all prophetic expectation. However, within the broader biblical narrative, several prophets are highlighted for their foundational roles: Moses is revered for leading Israel out of Egypt and delivering the Law; Isaiah is celebrated for his profound theological insights and messianic prophecies; Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and others also hold significant places in the canon. Different Christian traditions may emphasize various prophets differently, but the consensus tends to regard Jesus as the culmination of prophetic revelation.
